description: Ceiling on one run's checkpoint store. Crossing it stops the run and alerts instead of filling the disk.
read_by: the runtime, before each checkpoint write
note: Added after a runaway loop wrote a 90 GB checkpoint database on 2026-08-31 and took the server to 93% full.

description: Hard ceiling on how many graph steps ONE run may execute, loops included. It is the backstop above every per-step loop_ceiling: a 48-step flow whose loops all run to their limit stays far below it, and a routing bug that would otherwise spin for ever hits it and stops.
read_by: the runtime, as the graph recursion limit on every invoke and resume
ruling: Interface proposal during the phase A build, #6490
note: The 2026-08-31 runaway that wrote 90 GB of checkpoints had no ceiling of this kind. Per-step loop_ceiling bounds ONE loop; this bounds the whole run.

description: How long ONE Telegram long-poll waits before asking again. This is the worst-case delay between Yakov pressing a button and the run moving. Measured 2026-08-31 at 25 seconds: the answered gates showed waits of 24, 40 and 51 seconds - multiples of the cycle, not of Yakov. Three seconds costs about twenty requests a minute, far inside Telegram's limits, and makes the button feel immediate.
ruling: Interface proposal during the phase A build, #6534
note: Telegram's own getUpdates long-poll ceiling is 50s; 25 keeps a stop responsive.

description: How long a run waits at a human gate before it stops waiting and leaves the run paused on disk. The run is NOT cancelled - the checkpoint holds, and resuming it later is one command.
ruling: Interface proposal during the phase A build, #6490
note: A gate is a human decision; the default is a full day so a night does not kill a run.

description: Ceiling on one engine call made through the single engine wrapper.
ruling: Interface proposal during the phase A build, #6490

description: Largest single file the artifact store accepts on the host. Above it the run stops and asks, rather than silently parking something enormous.
note: Heavy files never enter git; this bounds what enters the host store too.

description: The file-size gate: no file this large or larger may enter a commit on the runtime repository.
note: This is the gate that stops a render or a CAD export slipping into the repository.

description: How many times ONE agent step may go round the think-call-a-tool-read-the-result loop before it must answer. The step ends with whatever it has; it is never cut off silently - the record says the ceiling was reached.
read_by: the agent loop in the engine wrapper
ruling: Interface proposal during the phase A build, #6506
note: Bounds cost and time per step. The run_step_ceiling bounds the whole run; this bounds one step inside it.

description: Ceiling on one local tool call - a fetch, a file write, a read.
ruling: Interface proposal during the phase A build, #6506
